scope.purpose: Design-only review of responsibility, Tag ownership and use, publication/display behavior, provider relationships, and sufficiency of compact intent.

assessed_commitments.assessment: SearchPanel owns helping the user find records using the provider-owned query vocabulary.
SearchPanel owns displaying search results for the current search.
Only the active request may publish search results. This excludes superseded-request publication without requiring additional response-order cases or a prescribed cancellation mechanism.
Cancellation is explicitly an implementation possibility, not a binding architecture choice.
SearchService finds records matching supplied text.

SearchService owns query and search results, accepts search text, and returns matching records ranked newest first. This provider commitment is compatible with the panel's display and publication commitments.

relationships.assessment: Resolved @search/service.sigil from the supplied original source root, then mapped the original provider path to its captured input. SearchService declares both selected Tags.
Both selected Tags have eligible exact bare references. The panel introduces no conflicting local identities. SearchService retains Tag ownership; SearchPanel retains ownership of its own Facets.
The import selects vocabulary. It does not independently establish a runtime call, transfer the provider's responsibility, or prescribe transport or request-management architecture.

coverage.compact_intent: The captured contracts are sufficient for the requested design scope. No evidenced contradiction, consequential missing obligation, unresolved final owner, or material simplification warrants a finding.
coverage.linked_context: Neither captured Sigil source contains an Inline Link requiring additional context.
omitted_scope: Implementation behavior, implementation conformance, and tests.
Product policy beyond the captured authored commitments.
Freshness of mutable original sources after this capture.

limitations: This is an independent advisory design review of the exact verified captured bytes; it is not human approval or a claim of saturated coherence.
No compiler or implementation validation was performed. Static reading of the selected sources does not establish workspace-wide language conformance.

Read-only and return-only restrictions were instruction-based; filesystem tools were unrestricted. No files were created or edited, and no compiler, network, evaluation fixtures, other evidence, or user-input tools were used.

Original files were not read. Before claiming coverage of current sources or applying a correction, the caller must verify all draft, provider, intent, and authority identities together with the source root and original-to-captured mapping.
